707031.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kahi, from earlier *kasi, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥t-, from *ḱóm (“with”). Compare Hittite 𒃰𒋾 (kat-ti, “along with”).

707066.t: The origin is unknown, with multiple theories proposed: * From a Proto-Indo-European *kaḱ-, *knḱ- (“slight”), and related to Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬯𐬎 (kasu, “small, slight”). * From Proto-Indo-European *kenk- (“to burn, hunger, desire”), and related to Lithuanian…

707097.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kalwós, probably from Proto-Indo-European *kal-wo-s, formed from *kal- (“beautiful”). Cognate with Sanskrit कल्य (kalya), Sanskrit क॒ल्याण॑ (kalyā́ṇa), Albanian kolmë.

707082.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱélh₂m̥ (“reed, straw”) via its zero-grade stem (such as genitive *ḱl̥h₂mós, with a shift in accent to *ḱĺ̥h₂mos), or (according to Beekes) independently thematicized from an original ablauting paradigm *ḱólh₂-m̥ ~ *ḱl̥h₂-ém-.

707049.t: From Proto-Hellenic *káwyō, likely from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂w- (“to burn”), with cognates such as Lithuanian kūlė̃ (“smut fungus ("burnt fungus")”), Latvian kūla (“old; dry; grass of last year”), and possibly Persian سو (su, “light”).

707042.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *kəňňós, from Proto-Indo-European *kn̥-yós, from *ken- (“new, fresh”).

707084.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kl̥h₁-, zero-grade of *kelh₁- (“to call”). According to Beekes, the term perhaps emerged as a back-formation from the aorist ἐκάλεσα (ekálesa).

707079.t: Variant of κάλαμος (kắlămos), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱolh₂-m-. Or from Pre-Greek.

707011.t: From κατα- (kata-, “down, against”) + ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to make stand, set up”).

707043.t: From καινός (kainós, “new”) + -της (-tēs, suffix forming nouns of state).

707005.t: From κατά (kătắ) + ἱζάνω (hĭzắnō, “to cause to sit”) with apocopic form καθ’.

707004.t: κατα- (καθ-) (“fully”) + ἱδρύω (“make to sit down; settle; found”).

707077.t: Compared by Beekes to γυργαθός (gurgathós, “wicker basket”), κύαθος (kúathos, “wine ladle”), and ὁρμαθός (hormathós, “cluster chain”) and declared Pre-Greek, likely based on semantic domain and suffix.

707070.t: Equivalent to κακο- (kako-, bad) + -ουργός (-ourgós, worker; maker).
